content: 1. The metabolism of calcitriol is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to an increase in its levels or effects. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels of ceritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ceritinib also increases the levels or effects of ritonavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of colchicine through mechanisms involving P-gp and CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Colchicine is a substrate of P-gp and CYP3A4. Avoid using colchicine with drugs that are both P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Colchicine use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels of dabrafenib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Dacomitinib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid using CYP2D6 substrates where even minimal increases in substrate concentration may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustments for dasatinib may be required. Both ritonavir and dasatinib inhibit CYP3A4, but ritonavir is a stronger inhibitor, increasing the risk of toxicity, including QT interval prolongation. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronedarone also increases the levels or effects of ritonavir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels of eletriptan by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 23. Ritonavir and elivaldogene autotemcel may decrease each other's effects through other mechanisms. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications, during their use, and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction. 28. Ritonavir increases the levels of ergoloid mesylates by decreasing their metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels of ergotamine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 35. Ritonavir and etravirine interact through other mechanisms, leading to contraindications. Different ritonavir preparations have varying effects on etravirine due to altered metabolism. The following preparations are contraindicated with etravirine: ritonavir 600 mg BID, tipranavir/ritonavir, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, and atazanavir/ritonavir. Lopinavir/ritonavir should be coadministered with caution. 36. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of everolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of felbamate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 40. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 41. Ritonavir increases the levels of flecainide by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone intranasal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs/symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence/severity of futibatinib toxicities. 46. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects and adjust dosage in cases of serious or life-threatening toxicity. 47. Givosiran increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, decrease the CYP2D6 substrate dosage as per approved product labeling. 48. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 49. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by decreasing their metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ritonavir both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 52. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
